title: Stoichiometry & the Mole
description: Molar mass, mole conversions, balancing, limiting reagents and percent yield.

questions.text: What is the molar mass of sodium chloride, $\ce{NaCl}$? (Na = 22.99, Cl = 35.45)
questions.explanation: Add the atomic masses of one Na and one Cl: 22.99 + 35.45 = 58.44 g/mol.

questions.text: What mass of calcium carbonate, $\ce{CaCO3}$, is 0.250 mol? (Ca = 40.08, C = 12.01, O = 16.00)
How many moles of water are in 36.0 g of $\ce{H2O}$? (H = 1.008, O = 16.00)
questions.explanation: Molar mass of $\ce{H2O}$ = 2(1.008) + 16.00 = 18.016 g/mol. Moles = 36.0 g ÷ 18.016 g/mol = 1.998 mol (about 2.00 mol).

questions.text: Write the chemical formula for calcium chloride.
questions.explanation: Calcium forms $\ce{Ca^{2+}}$ and chloride is $\ce{Cl-}$, so two chloride ions balance one calcium ion: $\ce{CaCl2}$.

questions.text: The limiting reactant is always the reactant with the smallest mass in the reaction mixture.
questions.explanation: The limiting reactant is the one that runs out first, which depends on moles and the balanced mole ratio, not on mass alone.

questions.text: Select ALL quantities that equal exactly one mole of carbon dioxide, $\ce{CO2}$. (C = 12.01, O = 16.00)

options.text: 22.4 L of $\ce{CO2}$ gas at 0 °C and 1 atm

questions.explanation: One mole is 6.022 × 10²³ particles, has a mass equal to the molar mass (12.01 + 2(16.00) = 44.01 g), and occupies about 22.4 L as an ideal gas at 0 °C and 1 atm. 12.01 g is the molar mass of carbon, not $\ce{CO2}$.

questions.text: Match each compound to its molar mass. (H = 1.008, C = 12.01, O = 16.00, Na = 22.99, Cl = 35.45)
For $\ce{2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O}$, how many grams of water form from 4.00 g of $\ce{H2}$ with excess $\ce{O2}$? (H = 1.008, O = 16.00)
questions.explanation: Moles of $\ce{H2}$ = 4.00 g ÷ 2.016 g/mol = 1.984 mol. The ratio $\ce{H2}$ : $\ce{H2O}$ is 1 : 1, so 1.984 mol of water forms. Mass = 1.984 mol × 18.016 g/mol = 35.7 g.

questions.text: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 12.5 g, but only 10.0 g of product is actually collected. What is the percent yield?
Which equation is the correctly balanced combustion of propane?
questions.explanation: Balance C (3), H (8), then O: 3(2) + 4(1) = 10 oxygen atoms, which needs 5 $\ce{O2}$. Option d has the right ratio of products but too little oxygen (10 vs 20 O atoms).
